subject: an online widget that would be nice to have

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: an online widget that would be nice to have
parts:
Hi, I was just editing a Stan model on Github, and I was thinking that it would be great if there were a button that I could click so that it would compile and run the model. As it is, if I want to do this, I need to download the model and the data and run Stan. So wouldn’t it be great to do it online? We could make it password-protected so we could afford the server time.

Perhaps this is a useful first step toward CloudStan, as it would be a tool that is not only cool but also directly useful for us.

A

I think that'd be nice. It wouldn't be hard to build, but
there's still the issue of how we'd get the model and data to the
online app.

I don't know what's become of the Julia implementation (we never
got the code or heard back from the developers), but we should probably
just forget about it and build something in Shiny since none of us
are Julia programmers.

Jonah's the natural person to do it, but he seems to be tied up
with applied problems for his employers and working with Andrew
on WAIC, hot hand, etc. Maybe he could teach me or Daniel enough about
Shiny that we could do it. I love building GUIs, but my plate's so
full it'd feed an army of developers.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] an online widget that would be nice to have
parts:
Is this really a Shiny thing? I mean, sure, it would be great to link this to Shiny, but for my current purposes, even a tabular output would be fine (wow—I can’t believe I just said that!). I just would love to be able to test out Stan models online on the Github site.

It would go like this: There’d be a mini-directory or zipfile with the following things:
- The Stan program
- The data (I’m not quite sure what format; we could discuss this)
Then on Github, I could push one button to compile the model and another to run it (with input boxes saying how many chains and how many iterations per chain). And I could alter the model or the data and try again.

This would make it so much easier for us to put example models up.

Another way to do it would be to have a mini-directory or zipfile with:
- The Stan program
- Data files
- An R (or Julia) script

But, to start with, I think maybe we just use CmdStan.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] an online widget that would be nice to have
parts:
We probably need to talk about this in person. I hate to
keep saying "no, it's more complicated than you think" to
everything Andrew requests, but that's just the way it is.

> On Jul 16, 2015, at 10:15 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>
> Is this really a Shiny thing?

Well, we need some way of building an interactive web site that
links to Stan, and Shiny seems like the easiest way to build a web
site with buttons. And if we do that, it should be pretty easy
to plug ShinyStan into it for rendering output.

> I mean, sure, it would be great to link this to Shiny, but for my current purposes, even a tabular output would be fine (wow—I can’t believe I just said that!). I just would love to be able to test out Stan models online on the Github site.

We can't run server processes on GitHub, so that's a non-starter.
We're going to have to build our own server and get Columbia to
give us a fixed IP address, or we're going to have to rent one.

> It would go like this: There’d be a mini-directory or zipfile with the following things:
> - The Stan program
> - The data (I’m not quite sure what format; we could discuss this)
> Then on Github, I could push one button to compile the model and another to run it (with input boxes saying how many chains and how many iterations per chain).

What do you mean by "mini-directory"? How do we nav
down --- I recall Andrew complaining that the models were
too hard to navigate on GitHub.

How would you like to see the menu of hundreds of models organized?
> And I could alter the model or the data and try again.

Or we could use the Julia thing if we can get the code
from Alan and Shashi.
> This would make it so much easier for us to put example models up.

How about doing it the way Allen did with Jupyter? There's no buttons
and it's not tied into our GitHub models, and it requires knowing one
of R, Python, or Julia, but we could probably build-in a bunch of selected
models.

> Another way to do it would be to have a mini-directory or zipfile with:
> - The Stan program
> - Data files
> - An R (or Julia) script
>
> But, to start with, I think maybe we just use CmdStan.

CmdStan vs. RStan isn't the issue --- it's a matter of building
a web server.

- Bob
